title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 131 (Voluntary revision of financial statements or Board's report)

content.overview: If it appears to the directors of a company that the financial statement of the company or the report of the Board do not comply with the provisions of section 129 or section 134, they may prepare revised financial statement or a revised report in respect of any of the three preceding financial years after obtaining approval of the Tribunal on an application made by the company in such form and manner as may be prescribed and a copy of the order of the Tribunal shall be filed with the Registrar.
content.glance: Board may revise financial statements or Board's report for any of the three preceding years for non-compliance with section 129 or 134, after Tribunal approval.
content.study:
## Section 131 — Voluntary revision

**When.** If directors consider that the financial statements or Board's report do not comply with section 129 or section 134.

**Window.** Any of the three preceding financial years.

**Approval.** Tribunal approval on company application in the prescribed form; copy of the order filed with the Registrar.

**Limits.** Detailed revision limited as the section provides (including once in a financial year in the applicable version); reasons must be stated.

**Distinguish section 130.** This is voluntary revision for non-compliance, not fraud/mismanagement re-opening under section 130.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Is section 131 the same as re-opening under section 130?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 131 is voluntary revision for non-compliance with section 129 or 134 after Tribunal approval. Section 130 is court/Tribunal-ordered re-opening on fraud or mismanagement grounds.
